title: First creation
transferTask: Add a different model somewhere else and explain how its position differs.

completion.title: You made your first scene
completion.explanation: You added, changed, tested, undid, saved and reopened a scene. Try the same idea on another object.
completion.why: You used the same edit, preview and save loop that creators use to build games and films.
hints: Replay the guide any time, or keep creating freely.
Try the same idea on another object without step-by-step help.

steps.title: Add an object
steps.explanation: A scene object is one placed thing. Add a model or an empty object to this scene.
steps.why: A scene is made from placed objects. Each one can have its own position and settings.
steps.completionFeedback: Object added. Select it and change its position.
hints: Look in the Add panel for a way to place something new.
Click Add empty object, or choose Browse for a model, preview it and click Add to scene.

steps.title: Change its position
steps.explanation: Move changes where this placed object sits. The reusable model stays the same.
steps.why: Position lets you arrange a world while reusing the same model in different places.
steps.completionFeedback: You changed this object's position. Next, predict what Play will do.
hints: Select the object you added, then choose Move in the Inspector.
With your object selected, click one of the X, Y or Z direction buttons under Move.

steps.title: Make a prediction
steps.explanation: Before you press Play, decide whether it changes your saved scene or a temporary copy.
steps.why: Predicting first helps you notice whether a test changes your saved work.
steps.completionFeedback: Right: Play tests a temporary copy. Now try it and stop.
hints: Think about what should happen to your saved scene when you test it.
Play tests a temporary copy. Your authored scene should still be there when you stop.

choices.label: The saved scene changes
choices.feedback: Play is temporary. Your authored scene remains available when you stop.

choices.label: Play uses a temporary copy
choices.feedback: Right: Play tests a temporary copy. Now try it and stop.

steps.title: Try the scene
steps.explanation: Press Play, try the scene, then press Stop to return to editing.
steps.why: Trying the scene shows how your change feels before you decide to keep it.
steps.completionFeedback: You returned to the authored scene. Think about what remained.
hints: Play and Stop are on the top bar. Stop returns to the authored scene.
Press Play, try the scene, then press Stop to return to the authored scene.

steps.title: What happened?
steps.explanation: When you stopped Play, what happened to the scene you were editing?
steps.why: Comparing the result with your prediction teaches you how preview and editing differ.
steps.completionFeedback: Yes. The test run was temporary, so your authored scene stayed intact.
hints: Compare the scene before Play with the one you see after Stop.
Play changes are temporary; stopping returns to the authored scene.

choices.label: My authored scene stayed the same
choices.feedback: Yes. The test run was temporary, so your authored scene stayed intact.

choices.label: Play edits were saved
choices.feedback: Stopping Play restores the authored scene; try that answer again.

steps.title: Undo the change
steps.explanation: Undo reverses an edit. Undo the move and watch the object return to its earlier position.
steps.why: Undo makes experimentation safer because you can return to an earlier edit.
steps.completionFeedback: The move was undone. Try a direction on a different object.
hints: Use Undo on the top bar, then check where the object moved.
Click Undo once and confirm the object returns to the position it had before the move.

steps.title: Try it on something else
steps.explanation: Change a different object. The same Move tool works on every placed object.
steps.why: Trying the same tool on another object shows the idea works across the scene.
steps.completionFeedback: You changed a different object too. The same tool works across the scene.
hints: Select a different object, then choose Move in the Inspector.
Select another object, leave Move selected, then click one axis direction button.

steps.title: Keep your work
steps.explanation: Save writes the objects and their positions into your project scene.
steps.why: Saving keeps the scene data with the project so you can return to it later.
steps.completionFeedback: Saved. Reopen this project to check that the scene comes back.
hints: Use Save on the top bar to keep your scene in this project.
Wait for the Saved message. If an error appears, fix it before reopening.

steps.title: Check it after reopening
steps.explanation: Reopen this project to check that the saved objects and positions return.
steps.why: Reopening checks that your project really kept the scene you made.
steps.completionFeedback: Your scene reopened with the same objects and positions. You can replay the guide or keep creating.
hints: Use Reopen this project below; it opens the current project without typing a path.
This reloads the project's startup scene and checks that the saved objects and positions return.
